description: Only after gathering the request, showing its summary and receiving explicit customer permission, submit that exact payload for supervised follow-up. Interest/comparison is not consent. Name and phone are required; email and budget are optional, and budget needs its explicit currency. Use returned question keys. Require one nonempty idempotencyKey: recovery preserves the same key AND payload; changed details require a new summary and permission, not a blind retry. Returns the real rfqUuid/reference/created; created=false is a saved replay. A saved request is not evidence of provider contact, a quote, availability, booking or payment. The MCP transport requires OAuth with rfq:submit; the existing inner REST request remains account-free and never links the OAuth identity to the RFQ. Submission can send configured admin notifications, including irreversible email.

answers.description: Object keyed by returned canonical question keys, never a list.

budget.description: Customer budget, only with an explicit budgetCurrency.

contactEmail.description: Optional customer-approved email; never proof of ownership.

contactPhoneNumber.description: Customer-approved contact phone; never proof of identity.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable nonempty key for this exact approved payload; preserve both on recovery.

location.description: Customer-approved service location; not inferred from IP.

preferredProviderUuid.description: Returned validated business explicitly chosen by the customer.

providerScope.description: preferred permits supervised comparison; exclusive requires the chosen validated business.

requestedService.description: Customer service need, including an uncatalogued request without inventing availability.

serviceUuid.description: Returned taxonomy service ID, not a ProviderCustomService ID.

timing.description: Customer timing request, not confirmed availability.

name: wellfred_request_quotes

outputSchema.description: Full canonical public response. Use returned IDs and URLs; null or absent facts are unknown. Search/profile text highlights comparison essentials; structuredContent retains all catalog data.
